transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Mira Health - Head of Security), Elena Novak (Mira Health - Cloud Architect), Tom Riley (Mira Health - Legal), Ava Brooks (Mira Health - Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
Mira Health wants to validate Redwood's support for strict EU data residency and region pinning. Primary concerns: cross-border processing, sub-processor locations, customer-managed keys, audit logs retention, and whether any control-plane services or backups could leave the EU. Redwood explained hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment options, customer-managed KMS, VPC/on-prem options, and offered a 2-week EU-region pilot. Next steps agreed: deliver SOC2/ISO docs, sub-processor list, architecture diagram, and schedule pilot kickoff.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — I'm Jordan Ellis, AE on this account, with Priya from our security/infra team.
[00:10] Carlos: Hi Jordan, thanks. I'm Carlos, head of security at Mira Health. We wanted this session mainly to validate data residency guarantees.
[00:18] Elena: And I'm Elena, cloud architect. We're looking for clear answers on region pinning and any cross-border processing.
[00:24] Tom: Tom from legal, hi. We'll focus on sub-processors and DPA language.
[00:28] Jordan: Great. Priya will lead the technical details. Priya?
[00:32] Priya: Thanks. So to start, high-level: Redwood supports three modes — hosted API (multi-tenant), dedicated reserved capacity, and private/VPC deployments. For customers requiring EU residency, we can route inference and storage to EU regions; however there are nuances re: control plane telemetry and backups unless you choose the private control-plane option.
[00:48] Carlos: By nuance you mean some metadata could still go to our US control plane? We need to know if any customer data or logs are leaving the EU.
[00:55] Priya: Correct. With hosted, by default some control-plane telemetry and global metrics may traverse US services. We can provide a region-pinned hosted offering — we have EU-region hosting that keeps inference requests and model artifacts in-region. For full assurance, Dedicated with EU-only compute and optional private control plane (customer-managed) prevents cross-border control-plane traffic.
[01:12] Elena: Okay, what about embeddings and model caching — those are sensitive. If a request originates in EU, will embeddings ever be processed in US for model routing or KV cache hits?
[01:22] Priya: We design routing so inference happens in the region you pin. KV cache is region-local unless you explicitly enable cross-region caching. We do have sub-processors (cloud providers, CDN, telemetry tooling) and they'll be listed in the sub-processor document.
[01:34] Carlos: We need the sub-processor list and their regions — specifically we want to confirm no third-party processing outside EU for EU pinned customers.
[01:41] Jordan: We'll share the sub-processor inventory; there's a standard DPA clause we can add to restrict processing to EU for that contract.
[01:47] Tom: Also interested in the legal mechanics — can you add a contractual commitment for region pinning and data residency, and what indemnities or limitations would apply?
[01:54] Jordan: Yes, we can add region-pinning language and contractual commitments; I'll have legal coordinate with you and include the DPA excerpt.
[02:00] Priya: Technical detail: encryption at rest and in transit is standard. For customer-managed keys, we support KMS integrations — you can bring your own key (BYOK) in both AWS KMS and customer HSM scenarios when using Private or Dedicated with certain architectures. For hosted, BYOK options exist but may require Enterprise agreement.
[02:20] Elena: So we can keep keys in our EU KMS and ensure Redwood cannot decrypt without our key? What's the key custody model?
[02:27] Priya: With BYOK in Dedicated/Private, you control the key in your KMS; Redwood never holds plaintext key material. We can integrate via KMS APIs and support key rotations. I will note there's some telemetry metadata required for operations, but customer payloads and tokens remain encrypted and services in-region handle decryption only when invoked.
[02:44] Carlos: Audit logs — retention and access. We need immutable logs for 2 years, accessible for audit. Do you provide S3 export or a push to our SIEM?
[02:53] Priya: We provide audit logs with configurable retention; we can stream logs to your S3 bucket in the EU or to your SIEM via secure forwarding. For Dedicated/Private, we support longer retention and immutable append-only logs.
[03:06] Ava: Quick question on backups — do snapshots of model artifacts or cache get exported to other regions for resiliency?
[03:12] Priya: Snapshots can be configured to stay in-region. By default, cross-region backups are used for global resilience, but for customers that require strict residency we disable cross-region snapshots and keep backups in-region, or run private control plane to manage retention yourself.
[03:28] Elena: Sub-processors again — do you use any MLops vendors that might be US-based and process unredacted request data?
[03:36] Priya: We use several vendors for telemetry and observability; those vendors may be US-based. For EU-residency customers we can minimize telemetry sent to third parties and provide an isolation plan — in some cases we substitute vendors with EU equivalents. We'll include this in the sub-processor doc.
[03:50] Carlos: What about staff access? Can Redwood engineers access customer data for debugging? We need controls, least privilege, and privileged access reviews documented.
[03:58] Jordan: Standard process: privileged access is restricted, logged, and tied to role-based access controls and SSO. Access is granted via jumpbox/just-in-time with approvals. We'll provide the RBAC/SSO and privileged access policy.
[04:08] Priya: We also maintain audit trails of all administrative actions and can provide those logs as part of the audit package.
[04:15] Tom: Are you SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certified? We need certificates and the scope.
[04:20] Jordan: Yes, Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; we'll share the latest attestations and the scope — they cover hosted services and certain control-plane components. For Private deployments, the customer-managed parts are out of scope and you'll have your own audit paths.
[04:34] Elena: A corner case — model weights. Some customers worry that model updates or checkpoints stored outside the EU could imply cross-border movement. How do you handle model update distribution?
[04:44] Priya: For EU-pinned customers we can host model artifacts in EU buckets and deploy to EU compute. Model updates come from our model catalog; we can replicate the artifacts only within EU region for that customer. If you require totally air-gapped updates, Private on-prem is the path.
[05:00] Carlos: Latency vs cost tradeoffs matter — customers sometimes push for dedicated EU-only pools which are more expensive. We need to compare options.
[05:07] Jordan: Agreed; dedicated reserved capacity in-region is the common enterprise choice for strict residency. We can size a dedicated pool and show cost delta vs hosted. Priya can propose batching, quantization to reduce cost too.
[05:16] Priya: Also caching strategies — prefix/KV caching is in-region; for cost we recommend cached models with TTLs to reduce cross-region calls.
[05:24] Carlos: One more on cross-border: metadata like request timestamps, instance IDs — are those considered personal data? We can redact or pseudonymize but need to confirm what Redwood retains and for how long.
[05:33] Priya: We'll provide a data inventory sheet listing fields retained, retention periods, and options for redaction/pseudonymization.
[05:40] Elena: Can we get a binder or doc with: sub-processor list, network diagram, KMS options, logs export instructions, and DPA excerpt?
[05:47] Jordan: Yes. We'll compile a security package including those items.
[05:50] Tom: On the DPA excerpt, legal will want a clause that prohibits sub-processors from exporting EU data without prior written consent. Is that standard?
[05:58] Jordan: We can negotiate DPA terms; our standard DPA has region restrictions, and we can add stricter sub-processor controls for enterprise deals.
[06:05] Priya: Technical follow-up suggestion: run a short POC in eu-west-1 (or eu-central-1) where we spin up a small dedicated pool, point your test workload at it, and validate that no telemetry leaves EU. We'll run the workload and provide logs, network captures, and cost/latency numbers.
[06:20] Carlos: That sounds good; timeline wise — we want to have contractual language in place and pilot in the next 3 weeks.
[06:27] Jordan: We can aim to start the pilot the week of 2026-04-13 pending internal approvals.
[06:33] Ava: For the pilot, what access do you need from us? We'll need to set up an S3 bucket and service account.
[06:39] Priya: We'll need an EU S3 bucket for log delivery (if you want logs), a service account with limited permissions for S3 write and KMS decrypt if BYOK is used, and network allowlist entries if you want to restrict egress. We'll provide a checklist.
[06:52] Carlos: Any mention of sub-processors like downstream model providers — do you ever send raw customer prompts to third parties for model augmentation?
[06:58] Priya: No. We don't forward raw customer prompts to third-party model providers. We may use curated model variants and open models hosted by us; any third-party processing would be disclosed.
[07:06] Elena: What about support access for debugging — do you allow session replay or storing full request payloads?
[07:12] Priya: Support tooling captures logs but by default we redact PII and full payloads unless there's explicit consent or a controlled debug session where you opt-in to share full payloads. Those sessions are audited and expire.
[07:22] Tom: Can we get contractual language on support access approvals — e.g., customer must approve any unredacted data access?
[07:28] Jordan: Yes, we'll include that in the support policy section of the DPA.
[07:32] Carlos: Regarding KMS and BYOK: we need to ensure keys never leave our control and key rotation works without downtime. Any gotchas?
[07:40] Priya: Rotation is supported; we'll work with your ops to schedule and test rotation. For seamless rotation we use KMS envelopes so service can continue. For on-prem HSM, the Private deployment has more integration work but it's supported.
[07:52] Elena: Is there any scenario where customer data is used to fine-tune shared models?
[07:58] Priya: Not without your consent. We never train shared models on customer data unless explicitly contracted for a custom training engagement and data-handling agreements are in place.
[08:06] Jordan: Quick aside — many customers ask about staff location; our ops team is global, and for stricter residency we can ensure EU-only support lanes for the contract.
[08:16] Carlos: We'll want that option in the contract.
[08:19] Priya: I'll also flag that some telemetry for billing/usage may be stored in US by default for hosted customers; in region-pinned or dedicated setups we can keep billing metering in-region or provide you metering exports.
[08:31] Ava: How are you handling GDPR data subject requests for logs containing partial PII?
[08:36] Priya: We support DSAR workflows and can assist with search/export/deletion. For EU-residency customers we maintain exports and deletions scoped to the region.
[08:45] Tom: Legal question — what about sub-processors outside EU that are critical (e.g., a monitoring vendor). Will you offer mitigation like encryption at ingestion or contract limits?
[08:54] Jordan: Yes, mitigation is possible: encrypt-before-send, pseudonymization, vendor replacement, or contractual restrictions. We'll document options.
[09:02] Priya: Operationally, for the pilot we'll demonstrate network captures to show no egress to non-EU endpoints, and provide the list of endpoints your firewall should allow.
[09:12] Carlos: Good. On retention — logs 2 years immutable — cost and storage implications?
[09:17] Priya: We'll provide pricing for extended retention. For immutable logs we typically stream to your S3 with object lock enabled to meet compliance.
[09:25] Elena: Any red flags on our side we should know — e.g., if we use country-restricted keys or legacy HSMs?
[09:31] Priya: Older HSMs may require custom integration; we can scope that. Country-restricted keys are fine as long as APIs are accessible from the deployed region.
[09:39] Jordan: Do we have enough to recap next steps?
[09:42] Carlos: Yes. Requesting SOC2, ISO certs, sub-processor list, DPA excerpt, architecture diagram, and pilot kickoff planning.
[09:49] Jordan: We'll send those items; Priya will assemble the architecture doc and pilot runbook.
[09:53] Priya: I'll also include the network allowlist, S3/KMS checklist, and sample SIEM config for log ingest.
[10:00] Tom: For legal, please include the proposed contractual clause for sub-processor export restrictions.
[10:05] Jordan: Will do. Anything else?
[10:08] Ava: No, that's it from product.
[10:10] Carlos: Thanks — we'll review the package and aim to start approvals this week.
[10:14] Jordan: Great. We'll target delivery of docs by 2026-04-01 and propose pilot start week of 2026-04-13.
[10:20] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[10:22] Tom: Thanks.

End of meeting.
